text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in Serbian and Montenegrin press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories nor does it vouch for their accuracy.
-- S E R B I A --
POLITIKA
- Yugoslav-Macedonian trade expected to reach $600 million this year, says head of Yugoslav delegation Vojin Djukanovic after bilateral talks in Skopje.
- The first phase of Montgenegro's privatisation to be completed by end of this year, some 55,000 citizens to receive privatisation coupons with a face value of 5,000 German marks.
- A new Danube tidal wave now in Bratislava will reach Yugoslavia in 72 hours. Population called to caution but emergency flood protection measures not necessary yet.

- Claims that Montenegro is not an equal partner in the Yugoslav federation means denying the existence of the federation, said Montenegrin President Momir Bulatovic in an interview to Serbian TV RTS.
NASA BORBA

- Ten opposition parties decide to boycott forthcoming Serbian elections and launch an anti-election campaign. One of the largest opposition parties the Serbian Renewal Movement has still not said whether it would join them.
- The Serbian parliament to discuss the privatisation law on Monday.
- Second round of Yugoslav talks with London Club creditor banks not expected to be held in July as planned, date of new meeting will probably be known on Thursday.
- Federal telecommunications ministry closed three private radio stations and one television station in Kraljevo over irregular licences.
VECERNJE NOVOSTI
- The Bosnian Serb constitutional court not expected to hold a public debate about the Bosnian Serb president's decision to disband parliament before August 10.

- Bosnian Serb President Biljana Plavsic welcomes her expulsions from the ruling Serb Democratic Party and calls for early parliamentary elections to oust from power two "slave owners" -- former president Radovan Karadzic and Serb member in the Bosnian presidency Momcilo Krajisnik.
POLITIKA EKSPRES
- Belgrade municipal court fines director of magazine Srpska Rec and wife of Serbian Renewal Movement leader Danica Draskovic with 80,000 dinars for libel against the daily Politika.
- Construction of 280 million German mark 68-kilometer railway stretch Valjevo-Loznica to be resumed. Foreign investors are showing interest in the project.
BORBA
- Yugoslavia's admission to the World Trade Organisation is a political issue, says Yugoslav Foreign Trade Minister Borislav Vukovic.
- The Yugoslav Left (JUL) has marked success in the country's parliamentary history in the three years since its establishment, says JUL spokesman at the party's anniversary celebration.
-- MONTENEGRO --
POBJEDA
- Montenegrin Prime Minister Milo Djukanovic opened car race Lovcen 97 in Cetinje on Sunday.
- Montenegrin railways open a computerised information centre in Podgorica. -- Belgrade newsroom +381 11 311 4305
